events.description: Ransacking of Pakistan's old mission in Kabul about nine months earlier, believed to be Masood's doing.
Taliban took Herat from the Kabul government, prompting anti-Pakistan anger in Kabul.

A crowd of 700 to 2,000, many armed with iron pipes and makeshift clubs, gathered at Zamaner Park around 9 am and marched to the Pakistani embassy chanting anti-Pakistan slogans. Shots were exchanged with guards, the chancery and residence were looted and burned, the fire spread to the British High Commission, one Pakistani was killed and four others were seriously injured. Ambassador Humayun was badly beaten.

Afghan envoy Masood Khalili told the US political officer that local security forces could not contain the mob and that Kabul regretted the incident; the officer expressed doubt that it was spontaneous.
Pakistan evacuated its embassy staff from Kabul to Rawalpindi by C-130 with Rabbani's approval.
Pakistan announced stronger security at Afghan missions in Pakistan, denied backing the Taliban and condemned the attack.

A mob of roughly 700 to 2,000 people gathered at Zamaner Park at about 9 AM and marched on the Pakistani embassy. They broke in, ransacked and burned the chancery and residence, and beat staff. One Pakistani was killed and four were seriously injured. Fire spread to the British High Commission.
Pakistan asked the Kabul government to provide additional security for its mission.
Pakistan evacuated its embassy staff from Kabul by C-130 to Rawalpindi.
Pakistan announced stronger security at Afghan missions in Pakistan. Its Foreign Ministry denied backing the Taliban and condemned the attack.
Envoy Masood Khalili told a US political officer that Kabul regretted the incident. He admitted some political elements may have been responsible but denied that Rabbani or Masood was behind it.
The Taliban captured Herat, which the mob blamed on Islamabad.

key_claims: A crowd of 700 to 2,000 gathered at Zamaner Park on 6 Sep 1995 and marched on the Pakistani embassy, blaming Islamabad for the Taliban capture of Herat.
Kabul security forces at a checkpoint did not stop the mob and reportedly tried to stop journalists filming it, suggesting complicity.

US post contacts believed the embassy burning could only have happened on the explicit orders of Ahmed Shah Masood, who was also believed to have been behind the ransacking of Pakistan's old mission nine months earlier.
Kabul envoy Masood Khalili conceded that 'some political elements' may have been responsible but denied that Rabbani or Masood were behind the attack.
Pakistan denied backing the Taliban and evacuated its embassy staff by C-130 to Rawalpindi with Rabbani's approval.
UN officials in Kabul said few residents have close ties to Herat, so its loss to the Taliban would not have caused a spontaneous outburst.
